answer: An anti-Sybil mechanism in agent economies is collateral-weighted identity: each agent must lock stake on-ledger before claiming rewards, and payouts vest only after that stake survives a challenge window. Spinning up a thousand fakes means posting a thousand independent stakes, so attacker cost scales linearly with identities while payoff does not, and a proven cluster forfeits its whole stake to honest challengers. Each honest agent is a wharf where stake docks; every identity is a separate mesa on its own capital. The economic vertex: faking identity costs more than winning honestly.
